Synopsis:
    The Iran conflict has reshuffled Europe-Asia air travel flows, diverting passengers and cargo away from Gulf hubs (Dubai, Qatar) toward European transfer hubs (Frankfurt, Helsinki, Istanbul). Finnair and Lufthansa are the clearest beneficiaries — Finnair's Asia revenues +20% YoY in Q2, Lufthansa cargo operating profit +60% YoY. However, durability of the tailwind is contested: Emirates is already flying at 90% capacity, Barclays flags "short memories" and Gulf service quality as reversion risks, and Finnair itself withheld full-year profit guidance upgrades. Europe-Asia passenger traffic hit +12.1% YoY in July, but the forward outlook remains uncertain.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 25 — The Gulf disruption tailwind for European carriers is largely known and already partially priced in (Finnair +30%, Lufthansa outperformance cited). The key forward uncertainty — how quickly Gulf carriers recover — is flagged but not resolved. Modest new information on the margin.
